about_seo_title: About Roots Tunisia — Carthage to the civil registry
about_seo_desc: Roots Tunisia preserves Tunisian lineage through Carthage, Kairouan, Ottoman sijillat, civil registry, and the 24 governorates.
about_hero_title: A Tunisian archive of names, places, and periods
about_hero_subtitle: From Punic Carthage and Fatimid Kairouan to Ottoman sijillat and modern état civil, Roots Tunisia holds family evidence across twenty-four governorates.
about_carthage_body: Punic stelae, Roman Africa proconsularis, and the Byrsa hill remain the oldest onomastic layer of Tunisian genealogy — names, places, and Mediterranean crossings that still echo in family memory.
about_kairouan_body: The Aghlabid and Fatimid capital preserved nasab chains, waqf deeds, and jurisprudential manuscripts. Kairouan remains a primary key for tracing scholarly and tribal lineages across the Sahel and the interior.
about_sijillat_body: Charaïque court registers, beylical decrees, and majba tax rolls document marriages, inheritances, and habous from Tunis, Sfax, and the medinas. These sijillat are the backbone of pre-colonial pedigree work.
about_civil_body: État civil from 1886 onward, Protectorate cadastre, and republican identity papers connect living families to the older documentary chain — 24 governorates, one indexed research surface.
about_mission_title: Why Tunisian genealogy needs its own house
about_mission_intro: Tunisian families are documented in more than one script, court, and language. A pedigree may begin with a CIN extract in Sousse, pass through a Tunis qadi sijill, and rest on a habous deed in Kairouan. Roots Tunisia keeps those layers together.
about_kairouan_panel_title: Nasab, waqf, and the Great Mosque
about_kairouan_panel_intro: Kairouan’s manuscript culture and pious endowments are not decoration. They are how families recorded descent, property, and scholarship from the Aghlabids through the Hafsids.
about_sijillat_panel_intro: Sijillat from charaïque courts, beylical chancery, and majba rolls name spouses, witnesses, neighbourhoods, and estates. They sit beside Protectorate état civil rather than beneath it.
about_habous_body: Pious endowments tying families to olive groves, fondouks, and medina houses.
about_etat_civil_body: Birth, marriage, and death registers from 1886, indexed by governorate.

terms_seo_desc: Terms of Service and conditions of use for the Roots Tunisia genealogical platform.
terms_intro: Please read these Terms of Service carefully before accessing or using the Roots Tunisia platform, archives catalog, or family tree building tools.
terms_s1_body: By creating an account, browsing records, or uploading family materials to Roots Tunisia, you agree to be bound by these terms, all applicable Tunisian laws, and international data protection standards.
terms_s2_body: You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your login credentials and for all activity conducted through your account. Family tree records may be set to public or private at your discretion.
terms_s3_body: Roots Tunisia provides citations and cataloging for civil status registers, charaïque court records, habous deeds, and municipal archives. While we strive for absolute documentary fidelity, researchers are encouraged to verify primary evidence.
terms_s4_body: Users retain full moral and intellectual property over family photographs, oral histories, and private memoirs uploaded to their accounts. Roots Tunisia claims no ownership over user-generated pedigrees.
terms_s5_body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Tunisia. Any disputes shall be submitted to the competent courts of Tunis.
privacy_seo_desc: Privacy policy and data protection guidelines for Roots Tunisia researchers and families.
privacy_intro: Roots Tunisia respects the sensitivity of family heritage and genealogical records. We are committed to protecting the privacy of living individuals and securing archival data.
privacy_s1_body: Details concerning living persons (born less than 100 years ago without death records) are automatically privatized by default and hidden from public searches unless explicitly shared by the tree owner.
privacy_s2_body: We collect account details (name, email, governorate/region), user-uploaded GEDCOM files, oral history recordings, and research inquiries submitted to our team.
privacy_s3_body: All genealogical databases and document stores are encrypted in transit and at rest, adhering to Tunisian data protection regulations and modern cybersecurity standards.
cookies_seo_desc: Cookie policy and session storage practices on Roots Tunisia.
cookies_intro: Roots Tunisia uses minimal, privacy-first cookies and local storage tokens exclusively to manage user authentication sessions and remember your language and theme preferences.
cookies_s1_body: Authentication tokens (JWT) and session cookies enable secure access to your private family trees, notes, and admin dashboards.
cookies_s2_body: Stored in localStorage under the key 'roots_locale' to display the interface in your chosen language (French, English, Arabic, Spanish, Italian, or Maltese). Duration: persistent.

why_roots_tunisia_title: Built for the Unique Depth of Tunisian Genealogy
why_roots_tunisia_intro: Tunisia stands at the crossroads of the Mediterranean. Tracing a family from Tunis, Sfax, Kairouan, Bizerte, or Djerba requires bridging Arabic, French, Ottoman Turkish, Italian, and Maltese archival records.
why_roots_tunisia_paragraph_2: Roots Tunisia unites municipal civil status registers (état civil), Sharia court marriage contracts (outul), Beylical tax rolls (majba), Habous family endowments, and oral histories in one scholarly workspace.
primary_evidence_body: Every person and lineage node can be linked directly to civil certificates, Sharia court deeds, or parish and consular acts.
territorial_depth_body: From the medinas of Tunis, Kairouan, Sousse, and Sfax to the oases of Tozeur and the island of Djerba.
period_context_body: Contextualize your ancestors across Aghlabid, Hafsid, Andalusian, Ottoman Beylical, Protectorate, and modern eras.

era_punic_detail: Phoenician-Punic maritime empire centered on Carthage alongside indigenous Amazigh Numidian kingdoms.
era_roman_detail: Rebuilt Carthage, El Jem (Thysdrus), Dougga, Bulla Regia, and Latin-African civic epigraphy.
era_vandal_detail: Late antique Christian basilicas, Byzantine fortifications from Kelibia to Sbeitla, and Mediterranean trade.
era_aghlabid_detail: Foundation of Kairouan and Mahdia, Great Mosque manuscripts, Arab-Berber genealogies, and ribats of Sousse and Monastir.
era_hafsid_detail: Tunis rises as capital; era of Ibn Khaldun, Zaytouna scholarship, and arrival of Andalusian families.
era_ottoman_detail: Muradid and Husainid Beys, Morisco towns of Testour and Zaghouan, Sharia court deeds, and the 1861 Constitution.
era_protectorate_detail: Standardized municipal civil status (1886/1908), censuses, Italian and Maltese Mediterranean communities, and the National Movement.
era_independence_detail: 1956 Personal Status Code, Patronage & Surname Law of 1959, universal civil registration, and national state-building.
era_contemporary_detail: Digitization of manuscripts and family archives, global diaspora reconnection, and collaborative GEDCOM genealogy.

dossier_title_all_tunisia: National Archival Atlas of Tunisia (24 Governorates)
dossier_summary_all_tunisia: Tunisia's genealogical heritage spans 24 governorates uniting Mediterranean coastal ports, Andalusian-settled valleys, Roman-Berber high plains, and Saharan oases.
dossier_settlement_all_tunisia: Successive Amazigh, Punic, Roman, Arab-Islamic (Aghlabid, Fatimid, Zirid, Hafsid), Andalusian Morisco, Ottoman Beylical, and Mediterranean layers.
dossier_holdings_all_tunisia: National Archives of Tunisia (Tunis), Municipal Civil Status Registers (since 1886), Sharia Court deeds, Habous waqf registers, and Beylical tax rolls.
dossier_summary_greater_tunis: Encompassing Tunis, Ariana, Ben Arous, and Manouba, Greater Tunis has served as the political, scholarly, and commercial heart of Tunisia since the Hafsid Sultanate.
dossier_settlement_greater_tunis: Punic-Roman Carthage, Hafsid Medina Beldi families, Andalusian artisans, Ottoman Deylical and Husainid elites, and Italian, Maltese, and Jewish urban communities.
dossier_holdings_greater_tunis: Dar el-Bey National Archives, Municipality of Tunis civil registers (from 1886), Zaytouna & Sharia Diwan archives, Bardo palace registers, and consular archives.
dossier_summary_north: Strategic Mediterranean port region anchored by Bizerte, ancient Utica, and the Andalusian-Ottoman naval harbor of Ghar El Melh (Porto Farina).
dossier_settlement_north: Phoenician Utica, Andalusian settlements in El Alia, Rafraf, and Metline, Ottoman maritime families, and 19th–20th century naval and Mediterranean communities.
dossier_holdings_north: Bizerte municipal civil status registers, naval arsenal archives of Menzel Bourguiba, Sharia court deeds of Bizerte and Mateur, and Habous agricultural endowments.
dossier_summary_north_east: Fertile peninsula of Nabeul, Hammamet, Kelibia, and Soliman paired with the mountain springs of Zaghouan — Tunisia's premier heartland of Andalusian Morisco heritage.
dossier_settlement_north_east: Punic Kerkouane, Roman Neapolis and Aquae Carpitanae, Byzantine Kelibia, and 17th-century Andalusian towns of Soliman, Grombalia, Beni Khalled, and Zaghouan.
dossier_holdings_north_east: Notarial deeds of the Caïdat of Cap Bon (Watan el-Qibli), Andalusian waqf endowments in Soliman and Zaghouan, and municipal civil status records.
dossier_title_north_west: North-West — Medjerda Valley & Numidian High Plains
dossier_summary_north_west: Uniting Béja, Jendouba, El Kef, and Siliana across the fertile Medjerda valley, Khroumirie forests, and historic fortress cities of the Tell.
dossier_settlement_north_west: Numidian royal cities (Dougga, Bulla Regia, Sicca Veneria), Andalusian Testour, Ottoman garrison lineages in El Kef, and Amazigh-Arab confederations.
dossier_holdings_north_west: Sharia court registers of El Kef and Béja, Testour Andalusian notarial deeds, Sufi zawiya manuscripts (Sidi Bou Makhlouf), and tribal tax censuses.
dossier_summary_sahel: Historic coastal belt of olive groves, Aghlabid ribats, Fatimid capitals, and ancient merchant towns stretching from Sousse and Monastir to Mahdia and El Jem.
dossier_settlement_sahel: Punic-Roman Hadrumetum (Sousse) and Thysdrus (El Jem), Aghlabid ribat scholars, Fatimid-Zirid Mahdia maritime families, and sedentary town lineages.
dossier_holdings_sahel: Municipal civil registers of Sousse, Monastir, Msaken, Ksar Hellal, and Mahdia; Sharia court deeds; olive-grove Habous deeds (Qanun al-Zaytun); and commercial registers.
dossier_summary_central_west: Anchored by Kairouan — fourth holiest city of Islam and capital of medieval Ifriqiya — alongside the Byzantine-Roman high steppes of Sbeitla (Kasserine) and Sidi Bouzid.
dossier_settlement_central_west: Roman-Byzantine Sufetula (Sbeitla) and Cilium, Fihrid and Aghlabid Kairouan scholar lineages, and major Arab-Amazigh confederations (Jlass, Majeur, Fraichiche, Hammama).
dossier_holdings_central_west: Great Mosque of Kairouan & Raqqada manuscript library, Sharia court registers of Kairouan, Sharifian nasab scrolls, and Caïdat tribal rolls of Kasserine and Sidi Bouzid.
dossier_summary_south_west: Spanning Gafsa, Tozeur, and Kebili around Chott el-Djerid — a storied region of prehistoric Capsian sites, palm oases, scholar-poets, and trans-Saharan caravan routes.
dossier_settlement_south_west: Capsian & Roman Capsa (Gafsa), oasis towns of Tozeur and Nefta (Bled el-Djerid), Nefzaoua communities in Kebili and Douz, and hydraulic lineage charters.
dossier_holdings_south_west: Oasis water-share deeds (partage des eaux), Nefta & Tozeur zawiya manuscripts, Gafsa Sharia court archives, and mining company civil & employment records.
dossier_title_south_east: South-East — Sfax, Gabès, Djerba & the Ksour of Dahar
dossier_summary_south_east: From the walled merchant medina of Sfax and the coastal oasis of Gabès to the island of Djerba and the fortified Amazigh hilltop ksour of Medenine and Tataouine.
dossier_settlement_south_east: Sfaxian merchant and architectural guilds, Gabès oasis families, Djerba Ibadi, Maliki, and ancient Jewish communities, and the Ouerghemma and JBalia ksour confederations.
dossier_holdings_south_east: Sfax notarial and family library collections, Djerba mosque & El Ghriba synagogue registers, Gabès civil registers, and Southern Military Territory (Affaires Indigènes) archives.
gov_desc_tunis: Capital of the Republic, historic seat of the Husainid Beys, ancient Carthage, and spiritual center of Zitouna University.
gov_notes_tunis: National Archives of Tunisia (ANT), Ottoman sijillat (1574–1881), majba registers, habous deeds, and central civil status from 1886.
gov_landmarks_tunis: Medina of Tunis (UNESCO), Ruins of Carthage, Bardo Palace, Zitouna Mosque
gov_desc_ariana: Northern metropolitan plain known for its historic Andalusian gardens, rose cultivation, and Beylical summer palaces.
gov_notes_ariana: Municipal civil status registers, agricultural land concession deeds, and historical records of the Tunis suburb caïdat.
gov_landmarks_ariana: Bir Belhassen Palace, Historic Borj Baccouche, Raoued Coast, Sidi Amor
gov_desc_ben_arous: Southern gateway to Tunis along the Gulf, home to Radès, Hammam-Lif thermal springs, Mornag vineyards, and Mount Boukornine.
gov_notes_ben_arous: Beylical palace registers of Hammam-Lif, municipal civil status of Radès and Hammam-Lif, and Mornag agricultural deeds.
gov_landmarks_ben_arous: Mount Boukornine National Park, Beylical Palace of Hammam-Lif, Radès Port, Uthina Roman Site
gov_desc_manouba: Fertile lower Medjerda plains, sanctuary of Lella Manoubia, Andalusian town of Tebourba, and historic Beylical Rose Palace.
gov_notes_manouba: Andalusian notarial deeds of Tebourba, Sufi zawiya manuscripts, military archives of Ksar El Warda, and Habous endowments.
gov_landmarks_manouba: Ksar El Warda (Rose Palace), Lella Manoubia Sanctuary, Historic Bridge of Tebourba
gov_desc_nabeul: The Cap Bon peninsula: ceramic guilds of Nabeul, Andalusian town of Soliman, citrus groves of Beni Khalled, and Kelibia fortress.
gov_notes_nabeul: Morisco/Andalusian settlement records (1609+), craft guild inheritance papers, Caïdat of Cap Bon registers, and Kelibia maritime rolls.
gov_landmarks_nabeul: Kelibia Citadel, Kerkouane Punic City (UNESCO), Hammamet Kasbah, Soliman Great Mosque
gov_desc_zaghouan: Mountain spring supplying ancient Carthage with water via the Roman Aqueduct, and historic Morisco haven famous for rosewater.
gov_notes_zaghouan: 17th-century Andalusian family papers, water-right & olive mill deeds, and Roman/Byzantine epigraphic records of Thuburbo Majus.
gov_landmarks_zaghouan: Roman Water Temple (Nymphaeum), Mount Zaghouan, Berber Village of Zriba El Alia, Thuburbo Majus
gov_desc_bizerte: Northernmost point of Africa (Cap Angela), historic port city, ancient Utica, and Andalusian-Ottoman harbor of Ghar El Melh.
gov_notes_bizerte: Municipal civil status of Bizerte and Mateur, naval arsenal registers, and Andalusian notarial deeds of Ghar El Melh, El Alia, and Rafraf.
gov_landmarks_bizerte: Old Port & Kasbah of Bizerte, Ichkeul National Park (UNESCO), Ottoman Forts of Ghar El Melh, Ruins of Utica
gov_desc_beja: Ancient Numidian Vaga, granary of Rome, nestled in the fertile Medjerda valley alongside Dougga and the Andalusian town of Testour.
gov_notes_beja: Sharia court registers of Béja, Andalusian notarial deeds of Testour, tribal rolls of Drid and Amdoun, and Dougga inscriptions.
gov_landmarks_beja: Dougga / Thugga (UNESCO), Great Mosque of Testour, Kasbah of Béja, Medjerda Valley
gov_desc_jendouba: Home to the subterranean Roman villas of Bulla Regia, ancient Numidian Chemtou, Tabarka coral coast, and Ain Draham oak forests.
gov_notes_jendouba: Souk El Arbaa / Jendouba civil registers, Khmir (Kroumirie) tribal rolls, and Tabarka maritime & coral-fishing archives.
gov_landmarks_jendouba: Bulla Regia Subterranean Villas, Tabarka Island Citadel, Chemtou Marble Quarries, Ain Draham Mountains
gov_desc_le_kef: Highland citadel city (Sicca Veneria) near Table de Jugurtha, historic cultural crossroads of Sufi orders, music, and scholarship.
gov_notes_le_kef: Sidi Bou Makhlouf Sufi zawiya manuscripts, Ottoman garrison & caïdat registers, Sharia court deeds, and Ghriba community archives.
gov_landmarks_le_kef: Ottoman Kasbah of Le Kef, Sidi Bou Makhlouf Mausoleum, Table de Jugurtha, Basilica of St. Peter
gov_desc_siliana: Highlands of the Tunisian Dorsal housing the Numidian-Roman city of Mactaris (Makthar) and the ancient site of Zama Regia.
gov_notes_siliana: Ouled Ayar and Kooub tribal records, Makthar Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions, and regional caïdat land registers.
gov_landmarks_siliana: Archaeological Site of Makthar (Mactaris), Zama Regia, Mount Serj National Park
gov_desc_sousse: The Pearl of the Sahel: Punic-Roman Hadrumetum, 9th-century Aghlabid Ribat and Great Mosque, and thriving coastal merchant city.
gov_notes_sousse: Sousse Sharia court registers, Msaken ashraf genealogical scrolls, olive-grove Habous deeds, and municipal civil status.
gov_landmarks_sousse: Ribat & Medina of Sousse (UNESCO), Great Mosque of Sousse, Kasbah Archaeological Museum, Takrouna Berber Village
gov_desc_monastir: Ancient Ruspina, 796 CE coastal Ribat fortress of Harthama ibn A'yan, textile guilds of Ksar Hellal, and birthplace of Habib Bourguiba.
gov_notes_monastir: Ribat endowment registers, notarial deeds of Monastir, Moknine, Jemmal, and Ksar Hellal, and Sahelian municipal civil registers.
gov_landmarks_monastir: Ribat of Monastir, Bourguiba Mosque & Mausoleum, Kuriat Islands, HistoricMedina of Moknine
gov_desc_mahdia: 10th-century Fatimid Caliphate capital on a fortified peninsula, renowned for silk weaving, Skifa Kahla, and the El Jem Amphitheatre.
gov_notes_mahdia: Fatimid and Zirid historical chronicles, silk-guild and maritime family deeds, and civil registers of Mahdia, Ksour Essef, and El Jem.
gov_landmarks_mahdia: Roman Amphitheatre of El Jem (UNESCO), Skifa Kahla Fortified Gate, Fatimid Great Mosque, Borj El Kebir
gov_desc_sfax: Southern economic capital with an intact 9th-century walled Medina, suburban borj garden estates (jnens), and the Kerkennah Islands.
gov_notes_sfax: Sfax family manuscript libraries, notarial deeds since the 17th century, Charfi cartographic lineage records, and Kerkennah registers.
gov_landmarks_sfax: Walled Medina & Bab Diwan of Sfax, Great Mosque of Sfax, Kasbah Museum, Kerkennah Archipelago
gov_desc_kairouan: Spiritual and scholarly capital of the Maghreb founded in 670 CE by Uqba ibn Nafi; seat of the Aghlabid dynasty and Maliki jurists.
gov_notes_kairouan: Oldest nasab lineage chains in North Africa, Raqqada parchment manuscripts, Sharia court registers, and Jlass tribal archives.
gov_landmarks_kairouan: Great Mosque of Uqba (UNESCO), Aghlabid Water Basins, Mausoleum of Sidi Sahbi (Abu Zama'a al-Balawi), Raqqada
gov_desc_kasserine: High steppe crossroads beneath Mount Chaambi (Tunisia's highest peak), encompassing Roman-Byzantine Sufetula (Sbeitla) and Cillium.
gov_notes_kasserine: Sufetula and Flavius family mausoleum epigraphy, Fraichiche and Majeur tribal confederation registers, and Thala caïdat archives.
gov_landmarks_kasserine: Roman Capitolium of Sbeitla (Sufetula), Mount Chaambi National Park, Mausoleum of the Flavii (Cillium), Haïdra Fortress
gov_desc_sidi_bouzid: Central agricultural steppes and pastoral plains around Mount Bouhedma, historic homeland of the Hammama confederation.
gov_notes_sidi_bouzid: Ouled Sidi Bouzid sharifian genealogy scrolls, Hammama tribal land and caïdat census sheets, and municipal civil records.
gov_landmarks_sidi_bouzid: Sanctuary of Sidi Bouzid, Bouhedma National Park (UNESCO Biosphere), Mount Mghilla, Historic Souk of Regueb
gov_desc_gafsa: Ancient Capsa — cradle of the prehistoric Capsian civilization — renowned for its Roman thermal pools, historic oasis, and mining basin.
gov_notes_gafsa: Gafsa Sharia court deeds, oasis water-distribution charters, Kasbah garrison records, and mining company civil registries (1897+).
gov_landmarks_gafsa: Roman Pools of Gafsa, Hafsid Kasbah of Gafsa, Selja Gorges (Redeyef), Mountain Oases
gov_desc_tozeur: Capital of Bled el-Djerid, famed for Ouled el-Hadef brick architecture, Ibn Chabbat's hydraulic canals, Nefta's Sufi zawiyas, and Abu al-Qasim al-Shabbi.
gov_notes_tozeur: 13th-century Ibn Chabbat water-share scrolls, Tozeur and Nefta zawiya manuscript libraries, palm-grove inheritance deeds, and caravan logs.
gov_landmarks_tozeur: Historic Quarter of Ouled el-Hadef, Corbeille of Nefta, Chott el-Djerid Salt Lake, Mountain Oases of Chebika, Tamerza & Mides
gov_desc_kebili: Heart of the Nefzaoua oases between Chott el-Djerid and the Grand Erg Oriental dunes, anchored by Kebili and Douz, Gateway to the Sahara.
gov_notes_kebili: Nefzaoua oasis property and water deeds, Marazig and Adhara tribal genealogies in Douz, and Southern Military Territory registers.
gov_landmarks_kebili: Douz Sahara Gateway, Old Town of Telmine (Turris Tamalleni), Ksar Ghilane Oasis & Roman Fort, Chott el-Fejaj
gov_desc_gabes: Ancient Tacapae: the Mediterranean's unique coastal palm oasis (Chenini, Jara, Menzel) paired with the Amazigh troglodyte hills of Matmata.
gov_notes_gabes: Mausoleum & madrasa manuscripts of Sidi Boulbaba, Jara and Menzel Sharia court deeds, and Matmata Amazigh family registers.
gov_landmarks_gabes: Mausoleum of Sidi Boulbaba, Maritime Oasis of Chenini Nahal, Troglodyte Homes of Matmata & Tamezret
gov_desc_medenine: Uniting the UNESCO World Heritage Island of Djerba, the coastal peninsula of Zarzis, and the vaulted ghorfa ksour of Medenine and Beni Khedache.
gov_notes_medenine: Djerba mosque & menzel family manuscripts, El Ghriba synagogue ketubot, Ouerghemma tribal registers, and Ksour property deeds.
gov_landmarks_medenine: Island of Djerba (UNESCO), Houmt Souk Forts & Menzels, El Ghriba Synagogue, Ksar Medenine & Ksar Hallouf
gov_desc_tataouine: Southern Dahar plateau famed for its multi-story fortified granaries (Ksar Ouled Soltane, Ksar Ezzahra) and hilltop Amazigh villages of Chenini and Douiret.
gov_notes_tataouine: Ouderna and Jbalia confederation registers, ghorfa granary ownership charters, Chenini and Douiret mosque manuscripts, and diaspora records.
gov_landmarks_tataouine: Ksar Ouled Soltane, Hilltop Villages of Chenini, Douiret & Guermessa, Mosque of the Seven Sleepers

about_methodology_title: From oral lineage to verified documentary trees
about_method_step_1_desc: We cross-examine ancestral nicknames, kunyas, and governorate origins against geographical registries and tribal confederation rolls.
about_method_step_2_desc: Court deeds, marriage contracts, and habous endowments establish unassailable legal parentage across centuries.
about_method_step_3_desc: Connecting 1886-present records with pre-colonial ancestry to render interactive D3 genealogical visualizations.
seo_periods_desc: From Punic Carthage and Roman Africa to Hafsid Tunis, Ottoman sijillat, the French Protectorate, and independent Tunisia — discover which records survive in each era.
period_punic_records: Votive stelae from the Tophet, Punic onomastics, Neo-Punic commemorative inscriptions.
period_punic_note: No unbroken lineage records survive, but ancestral names and territorial toponyms persist in Tunisian heritage.
period_roman_records: Funerary epigraphy, municipal alba, land surveys, El Jem and Dougga inscriptions.
period_roman_note: Latin inscriptions document family groupings, civic magistrates, and freedmen across Tunisian cities.
period_vandal_records: Ecclesiastical councils, episcopal lists, Christian Latin funerary texts, and fortress foundations.
period_vandal_note: Ecclesiastical records predominate; onomastic transitions reflect demographic evolution in urban centres.
period_aghabid_records: Kairouan biographical dictionaries (tabaqat), nasab lineage chains, early waqf deeds.
period_aghabid_note: Scholarly chains of transmission among Kairouan jurists provide Tunisia’s oldest continuous recorded lineages.
period_hafsid_records: Hafsid chancery registers, qadi court rulings, family endowment deeds (habous), and scholar ijazat.
period_hafsid_note: Tunis emerges as imperial capital; mercantile, scholarly, and Andalusian refugee families appear in continuous records.
period_ottoman_records: Charaïque court sijillat, habous deeds, beylical decrees, majba tax registers, and corporation rolls.
period_ottoman_note: The richest pre-modern documentary layer: inheritance and marriage cases systematically name three to four generations.
period_protectorate_records: État civil registers, cadastre land titles, caïdat files, Sadiki and school registers, ANOM records.
period_protectorate_note: Systematic civil registration begins in 1886; fixed family surnames become formalized across all governorates.
period_independence_records: National civil registry, CIN identity cards, nationality files, and municipal rolls.
period_independence_note: The Code of Personal Status unifies family law, creating modern verifiable civil lineages across Tunisia.
period_contemporary_records: Digitized civil databases, municipal registries, oral history testimonies, and archival restorations.
period_contemporary_note: Collaborative digital genealogy reconnects diaspora branches across the Mediterranean and beyond.

faq_title: Everything You Need to Know About Plans
faq_intro: Common questions on payments, data protection, and genealogy research tools in Tunisia.
faq_payment_q: How does payment work in Tunisia?
faq_payment_a: We accept Tunisian Dinars via Konnect, Flouci, Tunisian bank cards, postal cards (D17), and international debit/credit cards with instant digital confirmation.
faq_cancel_q: Can I cancel my subscription at any time?
faq_cancel_a: Yes. You can cancel your subscription with a single click in your account settings. There are no cancellation fees, commitments, or hidden penalties.
faq_gedcom_q: What is GEDCOM export and how does it protect my work?
faq_gedcom_a: GEDCOM is the global open standard for genealogical data. Researcher and Institution members can export their entire family database anytime, ensuring complete data sovereignty.
faq_privacy_q: How are my family records protected under Tunisian law?
faq_privacy_a: All personal genealogical data is securely encrypted and stored in private vaults in full accordance with the Tunisian National Authority for Personal Data Protection (INPDP).

need_help_sub_desc: Our specialized research desk in the Medina of Tunis is available to guide you.

guide_step1_desc: Present your National Identity Card (CIN) or Passport at the reception desk. A personal researcher card is issued on-site granting reading room access.
guide_step2_desc: Consult the paper inventories or online OPAC to find the archival classification (Série, Carton, Registre). Submit up to 3 call slips per research session.
guide_step3_desc: General administrative records become public after 30 years. Civil registry and judicial inheritance records protect personal privacy for 100 years unless direct ascendance is legally proven.
guide_step4_desc: Non-flash personal photography is permitted for most public series. High-resolution certified reproductions can be ordered at the digital laboratory desk.

aud_rec_2_place: Medina of Tunis — Souk des Chéchias
aud_rec_2_body: The chechia craft guild hierarchy, Amin regulations, and how noble Andalusian trade titles became official Tunisian family surnames.

aud_rec_4_body: Agricultural landholdings, colonial cadastral expropriations, and how family branches preserved oral nasab after 1956.
